claim: About 90% of Indonesian influencers' income comes from brand sponsorship contracts, meaning Southeast Asian creator income is structurally brand-deal dependent rather than platform-ad-revenue dependent as in the US YouTube model.
stance_target: The transferability of US creator income models built on platform ad-revenue share and CPM to Southeast Asian creators
scope_conditions: Indonesia; Vero Southeast Asia-wide influencer study, circa 2024-2025; SELF-SELECTED VENDOR SURVEY by a PR and influencer-marketing agency, sample under 50 Indonesian influencers, full methodology not disclosed; respondents are currently active monetising influencers, so severe survivorship bias
quoted_support: Today, as much as 90% of influencers' income comes from brand sponsorship contracts, the survey finds. In fact, 65% of respondents post sponsored content multiple times a week, while 24% post weekly.
numbers: 65% post sponsored content multiple times weekly

claim: Currently active Indonesian influencers rate the longevity of an influencer career at 4.10 on a five-point scale, above the Southeast Asian regional average of 4.02 -- but the sample is drawn entirely from survivors, making the optimism finding near-tautological.
stance_target: The use of active-creator surveys as evidence about the sustainability of a creator career
scope_conditions: Indonesia subsample of under 50 within a Vero Southeast Asia-wide study; vendor survey with undisclosed sampling frame; recruited from an agency network of monetising influencers; measures belief, not outcome
quoted_support: Among nearly 50 influencers surveyed from the archipelago, the average response was 4.10 on a five-point scale, slightly higher than the regional average of 4.02.

claim: Nearly 70% of surveyed Indonesian influencers planned to raise their sponsored-content rates in 2025 and 29% reported a lack of creative freedom in branded work -- the only located SEA creator-side data on pricing intent and job dissatisfaction.
stance_target: Characterising the friction points Southeast Asian creators report in brand work, as a partial proxy for quit-reason evidence that does not otherwise exist for the region
scope_conditions: Vero vendor survey, Indonesia, under 50 respondents, circa 2024-2025; measures stated intent and complaint, not realised rates or exits
quoted_support: Nearly 70% of respondents plan to increase their rates for sponsored content in 2025 ... However, 29% of the respondents said there is a lack of creative freedom when it comes to branded content.
